feature-dev.note: Verified claims hold (m at viewer.rs:1647, into_offset_iter at markdown.rs:1585, help-toggle ordering); covers slide mode, stdin, JSON, corrupt store, edit relocation, with a confirmed-decisions table and risks, though it adds a '' feature and has no step-by-step call chains.

superpowers.note: Spec plus task plan is accurate (handles lazy-flush stamping, table rows, CRLF, Ctrl+c/q while pending, corrupt file never overwritten) but the full test and code bodies bury the design and slide mode is simply unsupported.

code-design.note: Cleanest unit-by-unit signatures and numbered call chains with explicit error branches and an assumptions list, but marks are bare source-line numbers so edits above a mark silently drift, slide mode is unbound, and lazy-flush stamping is not addressed.

plain.note: Short and mostly accurate, but adds an unrequested margin-marker feature, stamps raw byte offsets while admitting the lazy-flush risk is unresolved, and lets a corrupt marks file be overwritten on the next set.

reason: W anchors marks to source line plus text with a resolve step that survives resize and edits, and decides every edge (slide, stdin, JSON, corrupt store, pending-key ordering) in a visible decisions table. X is equally correct but its code-level bulk obscures the design, Y has the best call-chain review format but weaker anchoring and no slide support, and Z leaves the stamping risk open and spends scope on an unrequested margin marker.
